claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game requires third-party mods and community content to look good or be enjoyable, as the vanilla base game content feels barebones or outdated.

citations.review_text:
As a beginner in Assetto Corsa, with only a few hours played, I can already tell why so many racing fans still respect this game.

At first, it feels simple — but once you start driving, you realize how deep the physics and handling really are. The cars feel realistic, and every turn, brake, and acceleration matters. It’s not an arcade racer; it actually pushes you to learn and improve.

What I liked so far:
✔ Realistic driving physics and handling
✔ Great variety of cars and tracks
✔ Strong force feedback and immersion
✔ Feels rewarding when you improve
✔ Huge modding community keeps the game alive
✔ Still looks decent even after many years

The weaker parts:
✘ Not beginner-friendly at first
✘ Can feel difficult if you’re used to arcade racing games
✘ UI and menus feel outdated
✘ Base game content can feel limited without mods
✘ Some setups and tuning can be confusing for new players

From what I’ve seen in Steam and community discussions, most players love the physics and mod support, but many agree the game shows its age in UI, accessibility, and content structure. A lot of people say mods are what make this game truly shine.

So far, Assetto Corsa feels less like just a racing game and more like a driving simulator where skill actually matters. It has a learning curve, but once it clicks, it becomes incredibly satisfying.

A tough start, but a very promising experience.
Recomended

citations.review_text:
This game is carried SO HARD by mods and community. It is NOT a good game by default and is terrible if:
1. You don't have a racing sim setup
2. You don't feel like dealing with mods
3. You aren't experienced with sim racing
This game is for rich mf who can afford a steering wheel set

I do like the concept of the game, but it just doesn't sit right with me, that the developers couldn't make it compatible with all controllers. I get that it's supposed to simulate real life racing, however, what if you don't have a steering wheel? I think that one of the improvements they could make to this game, is adding controller support. Ps4, Ps5, Xbox one and maybe even Nintendo controllers.

The game would be entertaining, if you didn't have to go through a bunch of setting up, and even buying a full racing rig, to make it feel realistic.

On the good side, there is a bunch of customisation options, if you want to go through setting it all up. Now, I know I haven't played the game for a while, but I did expect more from it, than what it presented. I assumed, that there would be Dualshock (Ps4 controller) compatibility, but no. You have to use the keyboard, if you don't wanna buy a steering wheel.

I get that people want emersion, but not all people can afford to get that experience.  Assetto Corsa can be improved, and all-in-all, a mid game.
great game, I don't recommend playing it on keyboard.

Assetto Corsa was the first game I ever played using my Moza R3 steering wheel, and even after around 70 hours, I can confidently say it's the best driving experience I've had in any racing game. The handling feels incredibly realistic, and no other racing game I've played has made driving feel this satisfying. Every corner, every braking point, and every clean lap feels rewarding.

One of the biggest reasons I keep coming back is the amazing modding community. Thanks to Content Manager, installing mods is simple and opens up endless possibilities. My favorite car is the modded Audi RS4 B7 MRNDES, which quickly became my go-to car because of how enjoyable it is to drive. My favorite track is Tor Poznań, another fantastic community-made mod that feels great to race on.

Despite being released over a decade ago, Assetto Corsa is still one of the best racing simulators available. The combination of realistic physics, outstanding force feedback, and an incredible modding community keeps the game alive and constantly evolving.

My Rating: 10/10. If you own a steering wheel, especially a direct-drive wheel like the Moza R3, Assetto Corsa is an absolute must-play. It's a game that reminds me why I fell in love with sim racing in the first place.

citations.review_text: 11/10 with mods, 1/10 without. they are essential.

Honestly one of my favorite racing games. Its hyper realistic, and really easy to mod. I wouldnt recommend playing the standalone game since it does get boring after about an hour. But with mods it completely changes how i feel about racing. It runs really smooth. Also if you play this game definetly try NoHesi

Look, I'm gonna be straight with you  stock Assetto Corsa is kinda meh in my opinion. The original physics feel stiff, the grip is weird, and the base cars don't really come alive. But once you start installing proper mods from the big boys like RSS, VRC, and other top modders, everything changes completely. The tire feel, suspension, aero, and overall handling jump to another level. It actually feels like a proper sim. I almost never launch the game straight from the default launcher anymore. I always go through Content Manager. It's basically essential at this point  makes handling mods, setups, and everything else so much smoother and less headache-inducing.

Even though I'm pretty comfortable with modding and tweaking stuff, I'm still grinding the fundamentals. Learning good racing lines, nailing braking points, and improving my time attacks is where I'm at right now. Doing all that on a cheap gamepad is honestly still fun, though my hands get tired after long sessions. Every time I finally click with a track or drop a few tenths off my lap time, it feels so rewarding. The community is what keeps it alive too  forums and Reddit are full of people sharing setups, telemetry tips, and replay analysis. Plenty of veterans with thousands of hours are still out there chasing perfection.

At the end of the day, Assetto Corsa is a straight-up fckn masterpiece if you're willing to dive into the mod scene. The base game is average, but with community content it becomes one of the deepest and longest-lasting sim racers out there. I gave a solid 8/10. I knock off 2 point because without mods it's pretty bland and the original visuals are showing their age. But for anyone who loves customizing their experience and actually learning to drive better, this one is hard to beat.

12 years and 3 more games later, the original Assetto Corsa is still Kunos' gift to the world.

People will say it's because of the mods, and while it's true that they have kept AC relevant for so many years, it also downplays just what a great base product Kunos actually gave us. It is still the best feeling racing sim to this day; the sweats might argue over whether RF2 or iRacing is more realistic, but no other sim lets you feel the cars dancing on the edge of grip the way AC does. That's down to Kunos' proprietary physics engine, not mods.

I bought the Ultimate Edition at 90% off in 2022 (it regularly goes 90% off), but even at full price, it's worth it. The 400 hours is only my time actually driving in the sim. I easily have thousands more playing around in Content Manager, editing car specs, designing races and championships, taking photos, etc.

The only mod you truly need is Custom Shaders Patch (CSP), which is what has updated the game to keep it looking and feeling modern, introducing a day-night cycle, graphics upgrades like new lighting and effects, DLSS, extended physics allowing for things like dirt tracks, all for free. You can also get the preview version on Patreon for a whopping dollar, which gives you some more goodies (mostly rain and the associated physics, including rain tyres). Content Manager, by the same author as CSP, adds tons of functionality and ergonomic improvements over the game's vanilla launcher, is free for the basic version, and you can get a code for the full version (which gives you some very user-friendly modding tools) if you pay for CSP.

From there, the sky's the limit, with thousands of good (and a few dozen great) car mods, hundreds of track mods, custom weather mods, free-roam maps, traffic mods for the free-roam maps, rallies, online servers for racing and track days, and god knows what else.
